title: India’s Javelin Deal: The Unending Loop of Procurement
gist: On August 28 the Indian Army signed a letter of offer and acceptance to buy US Javelin anti-tank missiles via the foreign military sales route, with US Ambassador Sergio Gor touting 'co-production possibilities'. The deal caps 16 years of stop-start efforts to fill India's anti-tank guided missile gap, and even now only piecemeal.

insights.claim: On August 28, the Indian Army signed a letter of offer and acceptance to purchase the Javelin anti-tank missile system through the US foreign military sales route, announced by US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor.
insights.so_what: A government-to-government FMS sale adds to US defense exports to India and supports demand for Lockheed Martin's Javelin line.
insights.quote: BIG news! India plans to buy the battle-tested Javelin anti-tank system
insights.speaker: Dinakar Peri

insights.claim: US Ambassador Sergio Gor said the Javelin purchase opens the door to 'co-production possibilities' in India.
insights.so_what: Potential local co-production would fit India's domestic-manufacturing push and could be a template for further US-India defense-industrial cooperation.
insights.speaker: Dinakar Peri

insights.claim: For the Indian Army, the Javelin deal follows 16 years of ups and downs to fill a critical anti-tank guided missile capability gap, and even now fills it only piecemeal.
insights.so_what: India's long procurement cycles leave capability gaps open for years, a structural constraint on its military readiness and on suppliers' revenue timing.
insights.quote: it marks 16 years of ups and downs and the long lead time to fill a critical capability gap in anti-tank guided missiles (ATGM), even if only piecemeal
insights.speaker: Dinakar Peri

insights.claim: The Javelin is a one-man-portable and platform-mounted fire-and-forget anti-tank precision weapon able to defeat all kinds of armor and fortified positions, in service with more than 25 countries including the US Army and Marine Corps.
insights.so_what: Broad international adoption makes the Javelin a proven, low-risk choice, and each new buyer extends the production base.
insights.speaker: Dinakar Peri
